name: Australia
sources: GDP $311bn current US$ and population 17.1m (World Bank national accounts, 1990).

Inflation 7.3%: ABS Consumer Price Index, year to 1990. Interest rate 0.175 is the RBA cash rate in January 1990, the peak of the tightening Keating used to break the late-1980s asset boom; it was cut through the year and reached about 12% by December, so this is a start-of-game figure rather than an annual average.

Tax 34% of GDP: total general-government revenue, ABS government finance statistics. Debt 22% of GDP: general-government gross debt was unusually low after four consecutive Commonwealth budget surpluses from 1987-88.
Defence 2.1% of GDP (SIPRI). Strength 14 reflects a 70,000-strong ADF built for continental defence under the 1987 white paper, with real naval and air reach in the near region and none beyond it.
Oil 0.6 mbd is 1990 crude oil production, chiefly Bass Strait and the North West Shelf; totals including condensate run nearer 0.68 mbd (BP Statistical Review).

Separatism 0.04 is residual Western Australian secessionism and unresolved Indigenous land rights; Mabo was still two years away. Stability 76: Hawke won a fourth term in March 1990 with the Labor Party's leadership succession already contested.
Investment shares: gross fixed capital formation about 25.5% of GDP in 1990, roughly 4.5% public and 21% private (ABS).
